clue.text: Meting out punishment with casual words

blocks.note: first meaning: what a judge does when announcing a penalty
second meaning: a remark made in passing, a throwaway line

explanation.surface: A stern figure dishes out discipline while chatting offhandedly.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase splits two ways: a judge's formal act, and a sentence spoken in passing.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge pronouncing a penalty is said to be doing this, and a remark tossed off lightly is also one.

clue.text: Hand over unacceptable permit for readmission

blocks.note: to pass something is to hand it over
out as in not allowed, out of the question

explanation.surface: Someone surrenders an invalid ticket that should let them back in.
explanation.definitionFit: A pass-out is the ticket or stamp that lets a spectator leave a venue and return later.

clue.text: Narrow outlook protected amid triviality

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: smallness is pettiness or insignificance
minded as in looked after, kept safe

explanation.surface: A sheltered person's horizons shrink among petty concerns.
explanation.definitionFit: Being petty and limited in one's views is exactly having a narrow, ungenerous outlook.

clue.text: Charge out; I'm in apt disguise

indicators.note: a disguise changes how something looks, so the letters appear in a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters of these words, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone protests an accusation: out with it, I am cleverly concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge out' looks like one phrase, but the definition is just 'Charge'; 'out' belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An imputation is an accusation or attribution of blame, the same sense as laying a charge against someone.

clue.text: After first prize, call for one of five Christmas gifts

indicators.note: after places the second word straight behind the first in reading order

blocks.note: gold is the medal for first place
to ring is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: A winner then phones to claim a festive present.
explanation.walkthrough: The carol The Twelve Days of Christmas has 'five gold rings' among the true love's gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: In the carol the giver sends five golden rings, so a single one is one of those five festive presents.

clue.text: Exploding mine on borders of territory shows ill-will

indicators.note: something exploding is blown apart, so the letters fly into a new order
the borders of a word are its two edges, its first and last letters

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
the outside letters of territory

explanation.surface: A landmine goes off at a frontier, a sign of hostility between neighbours.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmity is hostility or hatred, the same feeling as ill-will toward another.

clue.text: Measure runner's performance in centimetres

indicators.note: in means the answer lies inside the following word

blocks.note: sits in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A coach records how far an athlete went in a metric unit.
explanation.walkthrough: Centimetres suggests a distance, but the athlete's result is measured with a stopwatch.
explanation.definitionFit: To time an athlete is to measure how long they take with a stopwatch, recording their performance.

clue.text: Too trivial to risk one’s legs for

definitions.note: read literally, with pins as legs

blocks.note: first meaning: the idiom for something worthless
second meaning, taken literally: pins is slang for legs, so it is not worth staking a pair of them

explanation.surface: A cause too petty to stick one's neck, or legs, out for.
explanation.walkthrough: Pins is old informal slang for legs, which turns the idiom about a pin's tiny value into one about not risking a pair of legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means utterly worthless or of no value at all, describing something too trivial to bother about.

clue.text: Put in code for core of French underground cell

indicators.note: the core of a word is its centre, the letters in the middle

blocks.note: the two central letters of French
a crypt is a chamber below a church

explanation.surface: A spy hides the location of a Resistance cell in cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: To encrypt a message is to convert it into a cipher so outsiders cannot read it.

clue.text: Cut off top of head with edges of evil knife

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters

blocks.note: to scalp is to remove the skin and hair from the crown
the outside letters of evil

explanation.surface: A gruesome scene: someone wickedly slices off a head with a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalpel is a small, very sharp blade used by surgeons, a kind of knife.

clue.text: Copying some basic item immediately on return

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used
returning means going back, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters running across the word breaks

explanation.surface: Someone duplicates an everyday object the moment it comes back.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimetic means imitative, relating to mimicry, which is what copying something amounts to.

clue.text: Erase outside broadcast, getting left with repeat

blocks.note: OB is the standard abbreviation for an outside broadcast
L is the abbreviation for left
joins the last piece on
to iterate is to do or say again

explanation.surface: A TV crew wipes a location recording, leaving only a rerun.
explanation.walkthrough: An outside broadcast is a programme filmed on location rather than in a studio.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to wipe out or destroy all trace of something, a stronger synonym for erase.

clue.text: High-falutin’ trinket round front of neck

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter
round means going around, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: a toy is a small trifle or bauble
the first letter of neck

explanation.surface: A pretentious pendant hangs around the throat.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony is informal for stylish or upmarket; the necklace image hides that.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony is an informal adjective for fashionable and posh, close to pretentiously grand or high-flown.

clue.text: Did Ms Heliwell do nothing for music Down Under?

definitions.note: the answer is an instrument that makes the music

blocks.note: taken as written
Geri Halliwell, the Spice Girl, by her first name
taken as written
O is nought, zero

explanation.surface: A question whether a pop singer sat idle while Australian music played.
explanation.walkthrough: Geri Halliwell (spelt Heliwell here) was Ginger Spice in the Spice Girls. Down Under is Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The didgeridoo is the long wooden drone pipe of Aboriginal Australia, the source of that country's most distinctive sound.

clue.text: Dancing in serpentine style

blocks.note: first meaning: doing the Twist, a 1960s dance
second meaning: winding about like a snake

explanation.surface: Someone moves on the dance floor like a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The Twist was a popular 1960s dance, and a winding road or snake is also described as turning and coiling.

clue.text: Strict order to return child with shabby gear

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word is read in reverse

blocks.note: a kid is a child
tat is cheap, tatty stuff

explanation.surface: A parent firmly orders a youngster home in scruffy clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A diktat is a harsh decree imposed without consultation, a strict command from above.

clue.text: Course beginning to open data on cause of disease

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: a path is a course or route
the first letter of open
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A medical course starts by opening up the data on how an illness arises.
explanation.definitionFit: A pathogen is a bacterium, virus or other microorganism that brings about illness.

clue.text: Seemingly reserved for entrants under cover

blocks.note: first meaning, read whimsically
second meaning: inside a building, sheltered

explanation.surface: A sign marking a door for people arriving at a covered venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seemingly' flags a playful reading of the word as a door for coming in.
explanation.definitionFit: Indoor describes activities held inside a building, sheltered from weather beneath a roof.

clue.text: Temporary printer improving quality to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: straddles the gap between the two words
surface padding, completing the picture of better print

explanation.surface: A stopgap printer gives somewhat better output.
explanation.definitionFit: Interim means for the time being, provisional until something permanent arrives.

clue.text: Joyful sound as large hut's demolished

indicators.note: something demolished is knocked down and its parts scattered into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these words, taken as written

explanation.surface: People cheer as a big shed is knocked down.
explanation.definitionFit: Laughter is the happy noise of people laughing, a joyful sound by any reckoning.

clue.text: Russian force surprisingly ready to bring in Marines

indicators.note: a surprising outcome is unexpected, so the letters come out in an unexpected order
to bring in is to take inside, so one set of letters goes into the other

blocks.note: taken as written
RM is the abbreviation for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Soviet troops, unexpectedly prepared, enlist naval infantry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Army was the army of Soviet Russia, founded after the 1917 revolution.

clue.text: Hooligan against an upstanding youth

indicators.note: in a down entry, standing up means the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: V is short for versus, against
taken as written
a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A thug confronts a respectable young person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstanding' looks like praise for the youth but tells you to write that word upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal is someone who wilfully damages property, a kind of hooligan or lout.

clue.text: What may flow from thrashing out ideas

indicators.note: from means the answer is taken out of the words that follow

blocks.note: surface padding, part of the picture of a debate
runs across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A brainstorm in which good things emerge from hammering out thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrashing' is part of the surface only; the letters sit in the two words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide flows in and ebbs out, so it is a thing that may flow.

clue.text: What a state Dad's in!

blocks.note: surface: an exclamation that someone is in a terrible mess
setter's reading: the condition any father is in

explanation.surface: An exasperated remark that Dad is in a dreadful muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What a state' reads as alarm, but state here simply means condition: the condition of being a parent.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being a male parent is the condition every dad is literally in.

clue.text: Old boy with old English instrument

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
O is the abbreviation for old
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A former pupil turns up with a vintage English musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind, a familiar orchestral instrument.

clue.text: Rush to plant source of thatching material

blocks.note: a rush is a reed-like marsh plant
to bed plants is to set them in the ground

explanation.surface: Hurry to put in a crop that roofers will cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush' looks like a verb meaning hurry; here it is the waterside plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatched roofs are traditionally made of reeds, harvested from wetland stands of the plant.

clue.text: Less steady after prolonged turn

definitions.note: describes the state, an adjective phrase like the answer

blocks.note: first meaning: wobblier, less balanced
second meaning: how anyone feels once they have been spinning round for a long time

explanation.surface: A performer wobbles after a long stint on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' suggests a stage act, but it is literal spinning, which leaves a person dizzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dizzier means more unbalanced and wobbly, which is how a person is left after spinning for a while.

clue.text: My clue is: ‘One's all messed up in various ways’

indicators.note: something messed up is jumbled, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters of these words, taken as written
the letters of these words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter confesses that the whole clue has gone wrong in all sorts of ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks pretend the setter is apologising; the quoted words are the raw letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Miscellaneously means in a mixed or assorted manner, in several different ways.
